The fire started at 3 a.m. By dawn, it had consumed eight thousand acres. Firefighters from six counties converged on the ridge. They were outmatched from the start. The wind shifted. The flames jumped the highway. A mandatory evacuation order went out at noon. Twelve thousand residents grabbed what they could and left. Some took photo albums. Some took pets. Most took nothing. Captain Reyes had been fighting fires for twenty-two years. He said this one was different. The heat was more intense. The terrain was drier. Climate change is no longer a debate in these parts. It is a daily reality. Three homes were destroyed by nightfall. Miraculously, no one died. But the season is young. More fires will come. The question is not whether the next one will be worse. It is whether anyone will be ready.
